rendered:
The premise is reversed. The document reports that the lower-Mn sample, 10%[1] Mn, had the higher discharge capacity, not the higher-Mn sample. It gives 212 mAh g^− 1 (10% Mn)[2] versus 164 mAh g^− 1[3] for the higher-Mn sample, attributing the drop to the electrochemical inactivity of Mn4+ ions.

For heat release, the thermal decomposition tests show the same direction: the lower-Mn sample released more heat. The document gives 901.4 J g^−1 for 10% Mn[4] versus 485.7 J g^−1 for 50% Mn[5]. The lower-Mn sample therefore released 415.7[6] J/g more heat than the higher-Mn sample. The document attributes the lower heat in the higher-Mn sample to spinel phase formation, which it says improved structural integrity and delayed exothermic reactions in the lower-Mn sample.
